newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index ends sharply down in correction.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index ends sharply down in correction.

text.p: * All sectors fall, trading volume heavy
The Manila share index closed sharply down on Tuesday by 48.71 points, or 1.41 percent, at 3,398.89 points due to a correction phase, traders said.

"Finally, the market's expected correction happened today. It's quite healthy, brought about by profit-taking on most issues which have been overbought," said Nathan Lozada, assistant vice-president for institutional sales at Philippine Asia Equity.
In the broad market, decliners outnumbered gainers at 92 to 50 with 63 issues unchanged. Value turnover was more than twice the daily average at 5.3 billion pesos.
Among the most actively traded first-liner stocks which shed points were Philippine National Bank, Metropolitan Bank, Petron Corp and the Pilipino Telephone Corp.

Release of January inflation level on Wednesday expected to be lower than December 1996 and January 1996 figures may slightly perk up the market and cause the index to move sideways with an upward bias, Raul Ruiz, vice-president at Sun Hung Kai Securities said.
On Wednesday, the market may concentrate on Mabuhay Vinyl Corp which is listing shares after its initial public offering, brokers said.
The index will likely move within a 3,300 to 3,400 range within the week, Harry Liu, president at Summit Securities said.
Trading in secondary and tertiary stocks may be more pronounced in the coming days when investors are expected to sell ahead of the Chinese New Year celebration on Friday, Ruiz added.
